answers.core: This (to my knowledge) cannot be achieved with an add-on. It is also an unobtrusive feature, as those who don't want to use it can just not use it, and is a problem that many people seem to encounter.
answers.workaround: The three current solutions are the following: prefix the variable name with an underscore - this solution is fine, however, if I'm prefixing it with an underscore, that means I'm probably not going to use it, so why bother giving it a name rather than '_'; the second option is to mute the error globally, however, I believe this should never be done, as then what's the point in raising the warning; and third silence the error in that one instance using '#warning-ignore:warning_id', however putting this after every 'connect()' call is a rather untidy solution and feels unnatural.

title: Allow using `var _` to discard return values without raising warning `RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED`
